questions.question: Explain why the accounting equation A = O + L must be true at every moment, not just at year end.
questions.expected_answer: Every asset the business owns had to be funded from somewhere — either by the owner (equity) or by outsiders (liabilities). Since every transaction is recorded with equal debits and credits, each transaction preserves the balance, so the equation holds continuously; if it ever fails, an error was made.

questions.question: Describe the five-step self-check routine for analysing any transaction, and apply it to 'paid a creditor R5 000'.
questions.expected_answer: Name the two accounts (Creditors Control and Bank); classify them (liability and asset); decide increase or decrease (liability decreases, asset decreases); apply the sides (debit Creditors Control because a decreasing liability goes opposite its credit-increase side, credit Bank because a decreasing asset goes opposite its debit-increase side); confirm the equation still balances (A down R5 000, L down R5 000).

questions.question: In your own words, explain why buying equipment for cash needs two entries even though the accounting equation shows no net change.
questions.expected_answer: The equation's net change is zero only because one asset (equipment) increased while another (bank) decreased by the same amount. Both movements really happened and both must be recorded — debit Equipment, credit Bank — otherwise the individual account balances would be wrong even though the totals looked fine.
